quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: The difference in intensity between regular season and playoff players
quotes.excerpt: You realize the difference in intensity, the amount of focus it requires, how much more you have to raise your level.
quotes.quote: You realize the difference in intensity, the amount of focus it requires, how much more you have to raise your level than in the regular season. You start to see people fold. Guys who you've watched all regular season and they get in the playoffs and you're like, who is that? According to him, you have to be a certain level of physicality, and if you're someone that can't lock in on the game plan, you can't be a 16-game player. I thought last night, for the Warriors, you saw what a 16-game player looks like when it mattered most. It was one of the most fascinating things in sports to see that switch. When you're talking about switch flip, you're not just talking about physically showing, you're talking about mind, emotion, all of it. A different gear.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on the 'roach' vs 'moth' mentality in playoffs
quotes.excerpt: When the lights get bright, do you go towards it, or when the lights get bright do you go high underneath the fridge?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Are you a roach or a moth? And that's really it, right? When the lights get bright, do you go towards it, or when the lights get bright do you go high underneath the fridge? There's a lot of roaches in the league, and you know why they play good during the regular season? They are on boo-boo ass teams playing in front of 5,000 people like you're at some weird mid-major. When the lights get bright, they change the bulb for the playoffs. They don't use those regular bulbs, they put the halogen bulbs. This little light I got right here. When the playoffs happen, you're good and you're the only game that everyone is watching for the most part. So everything about your craft that you've been working on is seen. Are you ready for that moment? Are you fucking scared? Are you a roach?

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: You didn't have me at first.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: A coach told me that, and he said be a moth. Be ready to die to go into that light. So yeah, it got me hyped, but hey, it changed my whole attitude, because at the end of the day, you got to go down swinging.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on Derek Fisher as the ultimate 16-game player
quotes.excerpt: Derek Fisher at times, majority of his career, would look like one of the worst point starting guards in the fucking league.
quotes.quote: It's a guy that personally, I don't fuck with as an individual, but I'm going to give him his flowers as a hooper. When you talk about having that on and off switch, a 82-game versus a 16-game player for the post-season, that's fucking Derek Fisher. Derek Fisher at times, majority of his career, would look like one of the worst point starting guards in the fucking league. When it was time for him to step up and go into the post-season, alongside Kobe and Shaq or alongside Kobe and Gasol, that motherfucker stepped up to the plate. He instantly went from what? He would look, averaging six or seven points, that post-season come, that shit jumps to about 15 or 16 points per game, knocking down big shots, fucking game winners in San Antonio, huge moments defensive assignments like was built for that shit.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the pressure of being a starter at 22
quotes.excerpt: My rookie year, I'm 21 years old, we go to the finals, lose to the Lakers, we get swept.
quotes.quote: We know the stars that have won championships, they've proven. It's the players that can play around those stars that dictated. I'll tell you, my rookie year, I'm 21 years old, we go to the finals, lose to the Lakers, we get swept. That summer, they trade Keith Van Horn and now I'm starting. So now I'm starting at 22 years old and the standard is the NBA finals. So if we lose in the second round, it's like we shouldn't have traded Keith, we shouldn't have made this trade. This young player, if I got to the second round and my eyes got too big, if I got to the conference finals and my eyes were like, oh, what's going on? So that pressure is sitting on me all regular season.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Jrue Holiday as a consistent 16-game player
quotes.excerpt: Jrue Holiday is a 16-game player. We saw it in Milwaukee, we saw it in Boston.
quotes.quote: Jrue Holiday is a 16-game player. We saw it in Milwaukee, we saw it in Boston, we've seen it at different times in his. It's like he gets to the post-season, doesn't mean he's the most dominant dude, but he ain't the weakest link. He you know, and there's just a lot of dudes like that.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson's top 5 list of all-time 16-game players
quotes.excerpt: Bill Russell, MJ, Magic, Tim Duncan, and Steph.
quotes.quote: Bill Russell, MJ, Magic, Tim Duncan, and Steph. He won a bunch of game sevens, so that means to me that's the ultimate. I would say him, MJ, Magic, Tim Duncan, and Steph.

quotes.quote: LeBron is in that conversation. Kobe is in there for sure. That run after Shaq, he just rode that freaking ship off into the sale. Tim Duncan has to be in there.
